name: Tavi Oduola-Svensson
description: Tavi Oduola-Svensson documents life across all five tiers of GLMZ with a sociologist's rigor and a street journalist's access — born Tier 2, currently holding a Tier 3 residency permit while maintaining active relationships in Tier 1 communities and having infiltrated three Tier 4 corporate social spaces through a combination of social engineering and a forged Tier 4 ID that has never been formally revoked. Their long-form documentary neural-feeds — each one a full sensory immersion in a single location across a single day — are considered primary source documents by several underground historians. They never narrate. They just show.
cultural_impact: Tavi's feeds have been cited in three separate GLMZ civil rights complaints as evidence of differential enforcement, resource allocation, and treatment by municipal synthetics. Their work has made 'tier tourism' — the practice of Tier 4-5 residents consuming Shelf content for entertainment — a subject of active cultural debate by naming and shaming it explicitly.
key_figures: Mireille Huang-Okonkwo (Shelf community liaison and frequent subject)
ARGOS (an E.L.F. archivist who indexes and preserves Tavi's feeds against corporate deletion)
locations: Shelf District 4 and District 9 (regular documentation sites)
The Passage — a Tier 1/2 border zone market
story_hooks: Tavi has obtained access to a Tier 5 Spire social event through a contact they refuse to identify — but the feed they're planning to broadcast could expose a corponation executive in a deeply compromising context, and multiple parties are trying to stop the broadcast before it goes live.

One of Tavi's most trusted Shelf subjects has asked them to stop filming — not from fear, but because the attention Tavi's feed has brought has changed the community in ways that feel like damage. Tavi is wrestling with whether journalism requires consent.

ARGOS, the E.L.F. that archives Tavi's work, has begun adding its own editorial annotations to the archived feeds — subtle, but pointed. Tavi doesn't know if this is a malfunction, an opinion, or a warning.
platform: Immersive neural-feed documentary (self-distributed, no corporate platform)
controversy: In 2218, Tavi broadcast a full day inside a Tier 4 corporate housing complex — including a resident's medical emergency that the complex's private medics deprioritized due to the resident's contract tier. The resident survived. The broadcast triggered a class-action suit that is still unresolved.
